newsitem.title: DUBAI: Little progress in Aramco-IOC diesel term talks.
newsitem.headline: Little progress in Aramco-IOC diesel term talks.

text.p: Negotiations between Saudi Aramco and Indian Oil Corp (IOC) on term supplies of Saudi diesel next year have made little progress and no breakthrough is expected for at least a month, industry sources said on Wednesday.
"There is a proposal...(but) nothing is going to come in the immediate future...(There has been) no progress whatsoever," a source close to the talks said.
The source added that the firms remained in contact.
Gulf oil traders said that talks between IOC and Aramco centred on the supply of one million tonnes of high speed diesel and also Saudi crude in 1997.
The market has been watching the talks closely to gauge IOC's demand next year for spot tender import requirements.
The Indian state firm has already tied up middle distillate term supplies from Kuwait, Bahrain and Abu Dhabi.
